text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- World Bank extends $120 million credit line for primary education in Nigeria.
- The start date of the ALSCON aluminium smelter project has been put back to October 1997 because of lack of funds and raw materials as well as poor access roads.
- Chief of Army Staff, Major-General Ishaya Bamaiyi, accuses the Nigerian press of irresponsible journalism in propagating the views of foreign media, without questioning the foreigners' motives.
- Opposition National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) criticises a new timetable for elections, announced on Wednesday, as a ploy to keep military ruler General Sani Abacha in power.
- Traffic rules, which have varied from state to state since independence in 1960, are replaced by newly-released harmonised regulations.

- Former United States president Jimmy Carter in an interview with Voice of America radio says there may be division within Nigeria's ruling military council on the question of whether Abacha should stand for election in 1998.
- Workers at the troubled Ajaokuta Steel project may begin a strike to protest against the non-payment of five months salary arrears, which now amount to 165 million naira.
- A shipment of 12,000 tonnes of petrol is expected to arrive in Lagos on Friday.
